Reproducing Semenov et al. (2025), Figure S2, from dandiset 001271¶

Paper. Semenov I, Kim V, Silkuniene G, Pakhomov AG (2025). Excitation and polarization of isolated neurons by high-frequency sine waves in the context of temporal interference stimulation. Cell Reports Physical Science 6, 102660, doi:10.1016/j.xcrp.2025.102660.

Dataset. DANDI:001271, "Tetrodotoxin Blockade of Sodium Channels Abolishes Action Potential Formation During Intense Sinewave Stimulation", version 0.250805.1352, streamed from the archive. The paper cites the dandiset without a version, so the most recent published version is pinned. The earlier published version, 0.250701.1624, holds the same 287 assets with the same blobs (checked below), so the choice does not change the data.

Claims. claims/001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, written from the NIH author manuscript (NIHMS2098259, PMC12320893) with its STAR Methods and the supplement (Figures S1 to S4, Table S1). The dataset holds the Figure S2 experiment: neurons stimulated by 250-ms, 2-kHz sine waves before and about 5 min after the solution was replaced by one with 1 uM tetrodotoxin (TTX) or without it (vehicle). The claims file's other claims are on data in other dandisets (data: elsewhere).

The readings of the claims file's header (O1 to O5) are run in every combination. The whole 16 x 16 frame as the soma is shown beside them as a variant that does not decide an outcome.

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, header:
Method details fixed from the paper, used by the Figure S2 criteria.
(F1) F is the mean emission over the entire cell soma per frame, F0 the mean over an interval
before the stimulus, dF = 100% (F - F0)/F0 (Methods, Recording of the optical APs). FluoVolt
emission rises with depolarization, so traces are not inverted.
(F2) Traces are not filtered or modified in any way (Methods); no detrending or smoothing.
(F3) The stimulus is a 250-ms, 2-kHz unmodulated sine wave (Figure S2 legend), starting 50 ms into
the session (Methods); the onset, the field and the solution of each session are taken from the
dataset, and the 50 ms is used when the onset is not given there.
(F4) Sessions after the change are those about 5 min after the solution was replaced by TTX or
vehicle (Figure S2 legend); the solution of each session is taken from the dataset.
(F5) The maximum firing rate of a session is the inverse of the peak-to-peak interval between its
first two APs (Methods).
(F6) The two-sided Student's t test, paired or unpaired as appropriate, at p < 0.05, is the paper's
test where a criterion needs one (Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis). The paper
reports no test for Figure S2.

Details the paper leaves open, with the readings named. Every Figure S2 criterion runs every
combination of the readings below; a claim is decided when all give its outcome, and blocked as
methods_underspecified when they give different outcomes.
(O1) The soma outline is not given. ROIs are taken from the dataset when it holds them. When it
does not, readings (a) the connected component nearest the image centre (the Methods centre the
neuron) of an Otsu threshold of the mean pre-stimulus frame, (b) that mask eroded by 2 pixels, to
leave out the neurite bases at its edge. Otsu and the 2 pixels are standard choices.
(O2) The length of the F0 interval is not given ("a time interval preceding the electrical
stimulation"); readings (a) all frames before the onset (about 50 ms), (b) the last 20 ms before
the onset. This is unlikely to change an outcome.
(O3) AP detection is given only as "brief emission upticks", in neurons selected for APs above 5%
dF lasting about 10 ms (typical 11.3% and 8 ms). An AP is a local maximum of dF with width at half
height between 2 and 20 ms ("about 10 ms"; the bounds are a standard choice) and at least 5 ms
from a larger maximum (standard choice; the paper's highest rates, 60 to 90 Hz, give intervals
over 11 ms). Readings of the height (a) above 5% dF (the Methods' selection level), (b) above 5 SD
of dF before the onset. After TTX, (a) and (b) are applied with the level of the same neuron's
sessions before the change, so that a drop of the baseline noise cannot create APs.
(O4) "Sustained depolarization" is not defined by a measure. It is no AP in the last 100 ms of the
stimulus while the mean dF over that window is above, reading (a) 5 SD of dF before the onset,
(b) half the median AP height of the neuron before the change. The 100-ms window is a standard
choice. "Sustained firing" is, as a standard choice, at least three APs with one in the last 50 ms
of the stimulus.
(O5) Which session pairs are compared before and after the change is not stated beyond the
legend's "recorded first ... and again"; readings (a) every field tested both before and after,
(b) only the highest field tested both before and after.

Tetrodotoxin Blockade of Sodium Channels Abolishes Action Potential Formation During Intense Sinewave Stimulation
This dataset explores whether blocking sodium channels with tetrodotoxin (TTX) can prevent action potential formation during intense sinewave stimulation. Applying 1 µM TTX suppressed action potentials, as expected, and completely prevented sustained depolarization. This study was partially supported by the NIH Brain Initiative (NEI R21EY034803).

The files hold 16 x 16 frames, where the paper describes 64 x 64 pixels after 4 x 4 binning (Methods). Every file's first frame is about three times brighter than the rest and its last frame a few percent brighter than the one before; both are left out of every trace (sinewave.py). The images below are mean pre-stimulus frames: the soma fills most of the crop, so there is little background for a threshold to separate the soma from.

Duplicates and the identity of neurons across sessions¶

Each subject is taken as one neuron. Within a subject the sessions should show the same cell; between subjects, different cells. The mean pre-stimulus frames are compared by correlation.

In [7]:
print("distinct data arrays (SHA-1 of the frames):", s["sha1"].nunique(), "of", len(s))
wf = np.vstack([t["frame"][1:-1] for t in traces])
c = np.corrcoef(wf)
iu = np.triu_indices(len(wf), 1)
print(f"largest correlation of whole-frame traces between two different files: {c[iu].max():.4f}")
mp = np.vstack([m.ravel() for m in s["mean_pre"]])
cm = np.corrcoef(mp)
subj_arr = s["subject"].astype(str).to_numpy(dtype=object)
same_subj = subj_arr[:, None] == subj_arr[None, :]
within = cm[iu][same_subj[iu]]
between = cm[iu][~same_subj[iu]]
print(f"mean-frame correlation within subjects: median {np.median(within):.3f}, min {within.min():.3f} "
      f"({len(within)} pairs)")
print(f"mean-frame correlation between subjects: median {np.median(between):.3f}, max {between.max():.3f} "
      f"({len(between)} pairs)")
nearest_other = []
for i in range(len(s)):
    own = cm[i, same_subj[i] & (np.arange(len(s)) != i)].min()
    other = cm[i, ~same_subj[i]].max()
    nearest_other.append(own > other)
print("sessions whose least similar same-subject session is more similar than any other subject's:",
      int(np.sum(nearest_other)), "of", len(s))

Stimulus timing and the clock¶

The files carry no stimulus record. A 2-kHz sine sampled at 3,086.4 frames/s aliases to 1,086.4 Hz, and at high voltages it is visible in the images. Its envelope gives the onset and offset of the stimulus in sessions where it rises clearly above the pre-stimulus level. The contrast below compares AP-like peaks before the 50-ms onset with those during the stimulus.

In [8]:
rows = []
for _, r in s[~s["sham"]].iterrows():
    env = r["alias"]
    on, off = sw.frames(r["rate"])
    base = env[20:on - 20]
    during = env[on + 20:off - 20]
    ratio = during.mean() / base.mean()
    thr = base.mean() + 0.5 * (during.mean() - base.mean())
    above = np.where(env > thr)[0]
    above = above[(above > 20) & (above < len(env) - 20)]
    rows.append(dict(subject=r["subject"], volt=r["volt"], solution=r["solution"], ratio=ratio,
                     onset_ms=above.min() / r["rate"] * 1000 if len(above) else np.nan,
                     offset_ms=above.max() / r["rate"] * 1000 if len(above) else np.nan))
al = pd.DataFrame(rows)
clear = al[al["ratio"] > 1.5]
print(f"sessions with the alias envelope during the stimulus over 1.5 x its pre-stimulus level: {len(clear)} of {len(al)}")
print("their voltages:", sorted(clear["volt"].unique()))
print(f"half-amplitude crossings (10-ms smoothing): onset median {clear['onset_ms'].median():.1f} ms "
      f"(range {clear['onset_ms'].min():.1f} to {clear['onset_ms'].max():.1f}), offset median "
      f"{clear['offset_ms'].median():.1f} ms (range {clear['offset_ms'].min():.1f} to {clear['offset_ms'].max():.1f})")
print("expected from the Methods: onset 50 ms, offset 300 ms")
sham = s[s["sham"]]
print("sham sessions, alias ratio:", [round(float(r["alias"][160:900].mean() / r["alias"][20:130].mean()), 2) for _, r in sham.iterrows()])

ref = sw.measure(s[~s["sham"]], traces, "frame", "all", "5pct", "5sd")
pk_pre, pk_dur = 0, 0
for _, r in ref.iterrows():
    y = np.nan_to_num(r["x"], nan=0.0)
    found = sw.detect_aps(y, r["rate"], 5.0, 0, len(y))
    pk_pre += int(((found["frame"] >= 20) & (found["frame"] < r["onset"])).sum())
    pk_dur += int(((found["frame"] >= r["onset"]) & (found["frame"] < r["offset"])).sum())
pre_ms = (ref["onset"] - 20).mean() / ref["rate"].mean() * 1000
print(f"AP-like peaks (whole frame, 5% dF) per second: before onset {pk_pre / (len(ref) * pre_ms / 1000):.2f}, "
      f"during the stimulus {pk_dur / (len(ref) * 0.25):.2f}  ({pk_pre} and {pk_dur} peaks in {len(ref)} sessions)")

Field strength¶

The files say "1V translates to 36 V/cm". The fields marked in Figure S2 (vehicle neuron 45, 63, 72 V/cm; TTX neurons 90, 108, 117 and 54, 72, 81 V/cm) are compared with the voltages of the dataset's neurons tested both before and after the change, at 36 and at 18 V/cm per V.

In [9]:
fig_s2 = {"vehicle": [45, 63, 72], "TTX (a)": [90, 108, 117], "TTX (b)": [54, 72, 81]}
both = {}
for subj, g in s[~s["sham"]].groupby("subject"):
    b = set(g.loc[g["phase"] == "before", "volt"])
    a = set(g.loc[g["phase"] == "after", "volt"])
    both[subj] = (b & a, g["group"].iloc[0])
for name, fields in fig_s2.items():
    for k in (36, 18):
        volts = [round(f / k, 3) for f in fields]
        hits = [subj for subj, (v, grp) in both.items() if set(volts) <= v and grp in name]
        print(f"Figure S2 {name}: {fields} V/cm at {k} V/cm per V = {volts} V; neurons tested at all three "
              f"before and after: {hits}")

Readings¶

Every combination of the claims file's readings: O1 soma ROI (a otsu, b otsu_eroded), O2 F0 (a all, b last20), O3 AP height (a 5pct, b 5sd), O4 sustained depolarization level (a 5sd, b half_ap), and O5 session pairs (a every, b highest) where a claim uses pairs. The whole frame (frame) is a variant. Sham sessions are left out. Sessions where the O1(b) mask is empty have no trace under that reading and are dropped from it.

In [10]:
sw.READINGS["roi"] = ("otsu", "otsu_eroded", "frame")
stim = s[~s["sham"]]
M = sw.all_combinations(stim, traces)
M = M[M["x"].apply(lambda v: np.isfinite(v).any())].copy()
CLAIMS_ROI = ("otsu", "otsu_eroded")
KEYS = ["roi", "f0", "ap", "sdr"]
print("sessions per ROI reading:", M.groupby("roi")["path"].nunique().to_dict())
print("neurons per ROI reading:", M.groupby("roi")["subject"].nunique().to_dict())


def overall(table, col="outcome"):
    """The outcome all claims-file readings give, or the claims file's rule when they differ."""
    t = table[table["roi"].isin(CLAIMS_ROI)]
    vals = sorted(t[col].unique())
    return vals[0] if len(vals) == 1 else "readings differ: " + ", ".join(vals)

panels = []
for name, fields in fig_s2.items():
    volts = [round(f / 18, 3) for f in fields]

        if set(volts) <= v and grp in name:

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(panels), 6, figsize=(16, 2.3 * len(panels)), sharex=True, squeeze=False)
for row, (name, subj, volts) in enumerate(panels):
    for k, phase in enumerate(("before", "after")):
        for j, v in enumerate(volts):
            ax = axes[row, 3 * k + j]
            for roi, col in (("otsu", "k"), ("frame", "tab:blue")):
                g = M[(M["roi"] == roi) & (M["f0"] == "all") & (M["ap"] == "5pct") & (M["sdr"] == "5sd")
                      & (M["subject"] == subj) & (M["phase"] == phase) & np.isclose(M["volt"], v)]
                for _, r in g.iterrows():
                    t = (np.arange(len(r["x"])) - r["onset"]) / r["rate"] * 1000
                    ax.plot(t, r["x"], color=col, lw=0.5)
                    if roi == "otsu":
                        ax.plot(t[r["ap_frames"].astype(int)], r["x"][r["ap_frames"].astype(int)], "rv", ms=3)

                              f"last-100-ms mean {r['last100_mean']:.2f}%")
            ax.axvspan(0, 250, color="0.92")
            ax.set_title(f"{subj} {phase} {18 * v:.0f} V/cm", fontsize=7)
            ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
plt.tight_layout()

figs2-neurons-tested¶

The tetrodotoxin experiment was replicated in several neurons, with vehicle controls; the representative traces of Figure S2 come from at least 4 independent replications in different cells.

Readings: (a) at least 4 TTX neurons, (b) at least 4 neurons over TTX and vehicle.

In [12]:
sw.show_claim("figs2-neurons-tested")

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, figs2-neurons-tested

statement: The tetrodotoxin experiment was replicated in several neurons, with vehicle controls; the representative traces of Figure S2 come from at least 4 independent replications in different cells.

expected: [{'quantity': 'neurons in the TTX experiment, TTX alone or TTX and vehicle (readings in the criterion)', 'value': 4, 'tolerance': 0, 'unit': 'neurons, at least'}]

criterion: Neurons are counted from the dataset's subjects, sessions or cell identifiers, each recording counted once (author, step 1), and split into TTX and vehicle by the dataset's session metadata. The paper does not say whether the 4 replications count TTX neurons alone; readings (a) at least 4 TTX neurons, (b) at least 4 neurons over TTX and vehicle together. As a reported number read two ways, reproduced when either reading holds (protocol, step 3). The tolerance is 0 on a lower bound. The number of vehicle neurons is reported; the legend gives no count and the figure shows one, so at least one vehicle neuron is expected and its absence is reported as a finding.

Result: reproduced. The dataset holds 6 TTX neurons (two on each of three recording days) and 11 vehicle neurons with a visible solution change, so both readings (at least 4 TTX neurons; at least 4 neurons in all) hold. Three more neurons are labelled "without tetrodotoxin (vehicle control)" but show no gap of more than 3 minutes between sessions, so no solution change can be placed. All 287 data arrays are distinct.

figs2-before-firing-then-depolarization¶

Before the drug, unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves evoked repetitive APs at lower fields and, at the most intense fields, a sustained depolarization in which APs merged into small oscillations.

Sessions before the change, all 20 neurons (TTX, vehicle, and the three vehicle-labelled neurons with no visible change, whose sessions are all before any change).

In [14]:
sw.show_claim("figs2-before-firing-then-depolarization")

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, figs2-before-firing-then-depolarization

statement: Before the drug, unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves evoked repetitive APs at lower fields and, at the most intense fields, a sustained depolarization in which APs merged into small oscillations.

criterion: F1 to F3, under O1 to O4, sessions before the change only. Per neuron, the session at its highest field and its sessions at lower fields. Reproduced when every neuron (TTX and vehicle) has APs in some session, and more than half of them (a standard choice; the paper gives no fraction) show sustained depolarization (O4) at their highest field and APs without sustained depolarization at a lower field. The AP count and the maximum firing rate (F5) per session are reported against field.
In [15]:
B = M[M["phase"] == "before"]


def before_claim(g):
    out = []
    for subj, h in g.groupby("subject"):
        top = h[h["volt"] == h["volt"].max()]
        low = h[h["volt"] < h["volt"].max()]
        out.append(dict(subject=subj, group=h["group"].iloc[0], any_ap=(h["n_ap"] > 0).any(),
                        sd_top=top["sustained"].any(),
                        ap_low_no_sd=((low["n_ap"] > 0) & ~low["sustained"]).any()))
    o = pd.DataFrame(out)
    both_ = o["sd_top"] & o["ap_low_no_sd"]
    ok = o["any_ap"].all() and both_.sum() > len(o) / 2
    return pd.Series(dict(neurons=len(o), with_aps=int(o["any_ap"].sum()), sd_at_top=int(o["sd_top"].sum()),
                          ap_lower_no_sd=int(o["ap_low_no_sd"].sum()), both=int(both_.sum()),
                          sessions_with_sd=int(g["sustained"].sum()), sessions=len(g),
                          outcome="reproduced" if ok else "not reproduced"))

Does a sustained depolarization exist before the change, and can the O4 levels see it? Per neuron and group, at its highest field before the change: the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus and the two O4 levels. Two baselines without a depolarization share the frames, the bleaching and the F0 rule: the median of the same window over every session after TTX in that ROI reading (no APs, the bleaching drift alone), and the neuron's sham sessions where it has any. The depolarization over the TTX baseline is set against the O4(a) level (F0 over all pre-onset frames, 5% height).

sham = s[s["sham"]]
rows = []
for roi in ("otsu", "otsu_eroded", "frame"):
    m = B[(B["roi"] == roi) & (B["f0"] == "all") & (B["ap"] == "5pct")]
    m5, mh = m[m["sdr"] == "5sd"], m[m["sdr"] == "half_ap"].set_index("path")
    ttx_base = M[(M["roi"] == roi) & (M["f0"] == "all") & (M["ap"] == "5pct") & (M["sdr"] == "5sd")
                 & (M["group"] == "TTX") & (M["phase"] == "after")]["last100_mean"].median()
    sh = sw.measure(sham, traces, roi, "all", "5pct", "5sd")
    sh = sh[sh["x"].apply(lambda v: np.isfinite(v).any())]
    for subj, h in m5.groupby("subject"):
        top = h.loc[h["volt"].idxmax()]
        shs = sh[sh["subject"] == subj]["last100_mean"]
        rows.append(dict(roi=roi, subject=subj, group=top["group"], top_volt=top["volt"], top_last100=top["last100_mean"],
                         ap_in_last100=top["ap_in_last100"], level_5sd=top["sd_dep_level"],
                         level_half_ap=mh.loc[top["path"], "sd_dep_level"], ttx_baseline=ttx_base,
                         sham_last100=shs.mean() if len(shs) else np.nan))
DEP = pd.DataFrame(rows)
DEP["over_baseline"] = DEP["top_last100"] - DEP["ttx_baseline"]
print(DEP[DEP["roi"] == "otsu"].drop(columns="roi").round(2).to_string(index=False))
summ = []
for (roi, grp), d in DEP.groupby(["roi", "group"]):
    summ.append(dict(roi=roi, group=grp, neurons=len(d), ttx_baseline=d["ttx_baseline"].iloc[0],
                     median_top=d["top_last100"].median(), top_above_baseline=int((d["over_baseline"] > 0).sum()),
                     median_over_baseline=d["over_baseline"].median(),
                     median_level_5sd=d["level_5sd"].median(), median_level_half_ap=d["level_half_ap"].median(),
                     top_above_5sd=int((d["top_last100"] > d["level_5sd"]).sum()),
                     top_above_half_ap=int((d["top_last100"] > d["level_half_ap"]).sum()),
                     over_baseline_above_5sd=int((d["over_baseline"] > d["level_5sd"]).sum()),
                     over_baseline_above_half_ap=int((d["over_baseline"] > d["level_half_ap"]).sum())))
print(pd.DataFrame(summ).round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("sham sessions (subject, mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus window, O1(a)):",
      sw.measure(sham, traces, "otsu", "all", "5pct", "5sd")[["subject", "last100_mean"]].round(2).values.tolist())

d = DEP[DEP["roi"] == "otsu"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 10, figsize=(18, 4.2), sharex=True)
for ax, (_, r) in zip(axes.ravel(), d.iterrows()):
    g = B[(B["roi"] == "otsu") & (B["f0"] == "all") & (B["ap"] == "5pct") & (B["sdr"] == "5sd") & (B["subject"] == r["subject"])]
    for v, col in ((r["top_volt"], "k"), (g["volt"].min(), "tab:blue")):
        for _, q in g[np.isclose(g["volt"], v)].head(1).iterrows():
            t = (np.arange(len(q["x"])) - q["onset"]) / q["rate"] * 1000
            ax.plot(t, q["x"], color=col, lw=0.5)
    ax.axhline(r["level_5sd"], color="tab:red", ls="--", lw=0.7)
    ax.axhline(r["ttx_baseline"], color="tab:green", ls=":", lw=0.7)
    ax.axvspan(150, 250, color="0.9")
    ax.set_title(f"{r['subject']} ({r['group']})\n{r['top_volt']:g} V black, {g['volt'].min():g} V blue", fontsize=6)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
fig.suptitle("Highest (black) and lowest (blue) field before the change, O1(a); grey the last 100 ms, red the O4(a) level, "
             "green the after-TTX baseline", fontsize=8)

Result: not reproduced. Under each of the 16 combinations of the claims file's readings the criterion gives not reproduced (table above; the other 8 rows are the whole-frame variant, which fails too), and the criterion has no partial outcome. Firing before the change does not hold under every reading: with O1(a) every neuron fires with the 5% height (20 of 20), and 18 or 19 of 20 with the 5-SD height; with O1(b) all 7 fire with the 5% height and 1 of 7 with the 5-SD height. APs without sustained depolarization occur at a lower field in 18 to 20 neurons under O1(a). Under no reading does any neuron show sustained depolarization (O4) at its highest field (0 of 20, and 0 of 7 neurons under O1(b)), where the criterion needs more than half. At the highest field the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus is above zero in all 20 neurons (median 2.63% with O1(a)), but below both O4 levels (medians 7.29% and 4.93%), and in 9 of the 20 an AP still falls in that window. The whole-frame variant gives 1 of 20. Against a baseline without depolarization, the median of the same window in every session after TTX (-0.60%, as in the 5 sham sessions, -0.54 to -1.14%), the highest field raises dF in 20 of 20 neurons, by 1.15 to 6.01 points with O1(a), and in every neuron this rise is below both of its O4 levels. A depolarization is present but smaller than the levels of the claims file's measure, which cannot detect plateaus of this size in these recordings: the failed part says that this measure finds no sustained depolarization, not that the data show none. The outcome is therefore not reproduced, as the round-2 and round-3 verifiers agree. Whether O4 suits these data is asked of a reader (questions/001271.yaml).

figs2-depolarization-reversible¶

The sustained depolarization induced by intense unmodulated sine waves reversed immediately when the stimulus ended, so it was not membrane electroporation, which would take seconds or longer to repair.

Sessions with sustained depolarization (O4), before the change and in vehicle neurons. Windows after the stimulus: (a) 10 to 40 ms after its end, (b) the last 40 ms of the recording.

In [19]:
sw.show_claim("figs2-depolarization-reversible")

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, figs2-depolarization-reversible

statement: The sustained depolarization induced by intense unmodulated sine waves reversed immediately when the stimulus ended, so it was not membrane electroporation, which would take seconds or longer to repair.

criterion: F1 to F3, under O1 to O4, all sessions with sustained depolarization (O4), before the change and in vehicle neurons. "Immediately" is not quantified; readings of the window after the stimulus (a) 10 to 40 ms after its end, (b) the last 40 ms of the recording (the Methods give about 90 ms after the stimulus). Reproduced when, in every such session, the mean dF in the window is below the O4 level of that reading. A further check, from the paper's "seconds or longer", is that F0 of the next session of the same neuron (20 to 60 s later) is within 10% (a standard choice) of the F0 of the session before; it is reported, not judged. Windows are standard choices; the claim is tested on the Figure S2 neurons, while the paper's sentence cites Figures 1 and 3.
In [20]:
def post_window(r, w):
    if w == "10-40ms":
        a = r["offset"] + int(round(0.010 * r["rate"]))
        b = r["offset"] + int(round(0.040 * r["rate"]))
    else:
        b = len(r["x"]) - 1
        a = b - int(round(0.040 * r["rate"]))
    return float(np.nanmean(r["x"][a:b]))


rows = []
for key, g in M.groupby(KEYS):
    q = g[g["sustained"] & ((g["phase"] == "before") | (g["group"] == "vehicle"))]
    for w in ("10-40ms", "last40ms"):
        vals = [post_window(r, w) for _, r in q.iterrows()]
        below = sum(v < lv for v, lv in zip(vals, q["sd_dep_level"]))
        rows.append(dict(zip(KEYS, key), window=w, sessions=len(q), below=below,
                         outcome=("none qualify" if len(q) == 0 else
                                  "reproduced" if below == len(q) else "not reproduced")))
r3 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(r3.to_string(index=False))
print("\noutcome under the claims file's readings:", overall(r3))

Result: blocked (other). No session qualifies: under every combination of the claims file's readings, no session shows sustained depolarization (O4), so the criterion has nothing to judge. The whole-frame variant finds 2 or 3 qualifying sessions under its 5-SD readings, and in all of them dF falls below the O4 level in both windows after the stimulus.

Variant, not judged: at each neuron's highest field before the change, the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus and over the two windows after it (first reading and whole frame). And the reported check: F0 of each session against the session before it of the same neuron.

for subj, g in stim.sort_values("start").groupby("subject"):

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The claims file's readings give different outcomes. With the O1(a) ROI, no AP is found after TTX at the highest common field (O5 b), but over every common field (O5 a) one pair has a single AP after TTX: a 2.8-ms peak of 19.7 to 21.3% in a 14_20240731 session whose O1(a) ROI is one pixel (pre-stimulus SD 11.8%). With the O1(b) ROI, left with 3 TTX neurons, the 5% height finds peaks after TTX in 9 of 12 pairs, 2.0 to 3.9 ms wide, in ROIs whose pre-stimulus SD is about 3 to 12%; the 5-SD height finds none. In the whole-frame variant no AP is found after TTX in any of 31 pairs under any reading, against 215 to 253 APs before. Over every common field, the O1(a) readings find 158 to 204 APs before and at most 1 after. The plots show that single AP to be noise: the session's one-pixel ROI has a pre-onset SD of 11.8% with swings of about 40% throughout, and the peak (21% high) does not pass the session's own 5-SD level (58.9%). No session after TTX has an AP at its own 5-SD level under either claims-file ROI. The claims file's O3 sets the level after TTX from the neuron's sessions before it, so the outcome stays as its readings give it.

figs2-ttx-blocks-sustained-depolarization¶

Tetrodotoxin also fully blocked the sustained depolarization caused by intense sine waves, consistent with the depolarization arising from repeated activation of voltage-gated sodium channels by the cycling de- and hyperpolarization of the membrane.

Pairs of a TTX neuron where sustained depolarization (O4) was present before TTX. The criterion blocks the claim (other) when no TTX neuron has one.

In [26]:
sw.show_claim("figs2-ttx-blocks-sustained-depolarization")

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, figs2-ttx-blocks-sustained-depolarization

statement: Tetrodotoxin also fully blocked the sustained depolarization caused by intense sine waves, consistent with the depolarization arising from repeated activation of voltage-gated sodium channels by the cycling de- and hyperpolarization of the membrane.

criterion: F1 to F4, under O1, O2, O4 and O5. Per TTX neuron, the session pairs at the same field where sustained depolarization (O4) was present before TTX. Reproduced when, in every such pair, sustained depolarization is absent after TTX, and the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus after TTX is below the O4 level. "Fully" is read as that level; the mean dF over the window before and after is reported per pair, with a two-sided paired t test (F6) over pairs shown as a variant, not judged. Blocked (other) when no TTX neuron has sustained depolarization before TTX.

Result: blocked (other). The criterion blocks the claim when no TTX neuron has sustained depolarization (O4) before TTX, and none has under any combination of the claims file's readings. In the whole-frame variant one TTX neuron qualifies under the 5-SD level, and TTX removes its depolarization. Before TTX the six TTX neurons' highest fields raise dF by 1.15 to 6.01 points over the after-TTX baseline with O1(a), below both O4 levels in each, so the criterion's measure has no depolarization to follow through TTX.

Variant, not judged: the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus before and after TTX in every pair at the same voltage (O5 a), with a two-sided paired t test (F6) over pairs.

figs2-vehicle-keeps-response¶

In vehicle controls, recorded about 5 min after the solution was replaced by the same solution without TTX, the firing and sustained depolarization persisted.

Vehicle neurons with a visible solution change (11). Reproduced when every pair with APs before has APs after, and every pair with sustained depolarization before has it after.

sw.show_claim("figs2-vehicle-keeps-response")

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, figs2-vehicle-keeps-response

statement: In vehicle controls, recorded about 5 min after the solution was replaced by the same solution without TTX, the firing and sustained depolarization persisted.

criterion: F1 to F4, under O1 to O5. Per vehicle neuron, session pairs at the same field before and after the change. Reproduced when, in every vehicle neuron, every pair with APs before has APs after, and every pair with sustained depolarization (O4) before has it after. AP counts and the maximum firing rate (F5) per pair are reported; the paper does not say whether the response must be unchanged, so a decline is reported, not judged. Blocked (other) when the dataset holds no vehicle neuron.

                         pairs_ap_before=len(qa), lost_ap=lost_ap, pairs_sd_before=len(qs), lost_sd=lost_sd,

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The readings disagree. Over every common voltage (O5 a) some pairs with APs before have none after: 3 or 4 of 50 to 59 under O1(a), 1 of 9 under O1(b) with the 5% height (with the 5-SD height no O1(b) pair has APs before), and 2 of 59 in the whole-frame variant, so the claim fails there. At the highest common voltage (O5 b) every pair keeps its APs under the 5-SD height with O1(a), and 1 of 11 loses them under O1(a) with the 5% height. No pair has sustained depolarization (O4) before, so that part of the criterion is empty. Under O1(a) with the 5% height, vehicle neurons fire 334 APs before and 327 after over 59 pairs (p = 0.77). Per neuron, all 11 vehicle neurons fire after the change under O1(a) with the 5% height, and 8 of 11 keep APs in every pair that had them; with the 5-SD height 9 of 11 fire after it, and the other two have no AP before either. The change point of 13_20240801 is placed at its last gap over 3 minutes (5.0 min), not its largest (10.8 min), which would leave one session before; its sessions on each side of the 5.0-min gap repeat the same voltage series, so the last gap is kept. With the largest gap its lost pairs under O1(a) go from 1 or 2 to 0, which does not change the outcome, since the O5 readings still disagree in the other neurons.

ap-amplitude-duration¶

Neurons were selected for APs peaking above 5% dF and lasting about 10 ms; typical APs were 11.3% dF high and 8 ms long, excluding the afterhyperpolarization.

Per neuron, the mean peak dF and duration of its APs before the change; the mean over neurons is compared with 11.3 +/- 0.9% and 8 +/- 0.7 ms. Readings: which APs (all, or the first of each session) and the duration (width at half height, or rise to the return to F0).

In [34]:
sw.show_claim("ap-amplitude-duration")

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, ap-amplitude-duration

statement: Neurons were selected for APs peaking above 5% dF and lasting about 10 ms; typical APs were 11.3% dF high and 8 ms long, excluding the afterhyperpolarization.

expected: [{'quantity': 'mean AP peak over neurons', 'value': 11.3, 'tolerance': 0.9, 'unit': 'percent dF'}, {'quantity': 'mean AP duration over neurons', 'value': 8, 'tolerance': 0.7, 'unit': 'ms'}]

criterion: F1 and F2, under O1 to O3, sessions before the change. The paper does not say which 22 neurons these are or which experiments they come from; the neurons of this dataset are tested as neurons the same selection was applied to, and a mismatch may come from that. Per neuron, the mean peak dF and duration of its APs. Which APs are measured is not given; readings (a) all APs before the change, (b) the first AP of each session, which is not merged with others. The duration measure is not given; readings (a) width at half height, (b) time from the rise to the return to F0 on the decay, ending at the first crossing of F0 (so the afterhyperpolarization is left out). These readings are method details that can change the outcome, so the header's rule applies. Reproduced when the means over neurons are within the paper's SEM under every reading; partially reproduced when, under every reading, every neuron has APs above 5% dF and lasting 2 to 20 ms (O3) but a mean falls outside; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings give different outcomes. The number of neurons with APs above 5% is reported.

One reading (O1 a, F0 over all frames, 5-SD height, first AP of each session, duration to F0) gives means within the paper's SEM (10.76% and 7.62 ms over 18 neurons); the other 31 combinations of the claims file's readings do not. With the O1(a) ROI, mean peaks are 9.29 to 10.82% and widths at half height 3.56 to 4.06 ms; with the O1(b) ROI (7 neurons, 1 with the 5-SD height) peaks are 15.8 to 18.9%. fig3-not-heating (calculated, no data)¶

Excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating; the adiabatic temperature rise was 2.5 C after 250 ms at 63 V/cm in NaCl solution, at most 1.24 C for the same stimulus in the low-conductivity solution, and 4.1 C at 81 V/cm in NaCl.

The rise is sigma E^2 t / (rho c), with the heat capacity of water, E as (a) the peak and (b) the RMS field (criterion). The conductivities are the Methods' 16.4 and 8.4 mS/cm.

sw.show_claim("fig3-not-heating")

001271/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, fig3-not-heating

statement: Excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating; the adiabatic temperature rise was 2.5 C after 250 ms at 63 V/cm in NaCl solution, at most 1.24 C for the same stimulus in the low-conductivity solution, and 4.1 C at 81 V/cm in NaCl.

expected: [{'quantity': 'adiabatic rise, 63 V/cm, 250 ms, 16.4 mS/cm', 'value': 2.5, 'tolerance': 0.25, 'unit': 'degrees C'}, {'quantity': 'adiabatic rise, 63 V/cm, 250 ms, 8.4 mS/cm', 'value': 1.24, 'tolerance': 0.124, 'unit': 'degrees C'}, {'quantity': 'adiabatic rise, 81 V/cm, 250 ms, 16.4 mS/cm', 'value': 4.1, 'tolerance': 0.41, 'unit': 'degrees C'}]

criterion: The rise is sigma E^2 t over the volumetric heat capacity (reference 43, cited for the adiabatic assumption). The paper does not give the heat capacity or whether E is the peak or the RMS field; readings (a) peak, (b) RMS, each with the heat capacity of water (4.18 J per cm3 per K, a standard choice). Reproduced when all three are within tolerance under a reading; since these are calculated numbers read two ways, that reading is reported. Computed from the paper's own values (1.64 S/m, 63 V/cm, 0.25 s), neither reading gives 2.5 C (peak about 3.9 C, RMS about 1.95 C), while the ratios 4.1/2.5 and 1.24/2.5 follow the formula's scaling with E^2 and with conductivity. The heat capacity or field definition the paper used is therefore not known; when no reading matches the absolute values but the two ratios are within 10%, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified, and it is not reproduced only when the ratios fail as well. That the Figure 3A neuron fired at 63 V/cm in NaGlu as at 81 V/cm in NaCl is tested as in fig3b-low-conductivity-halves-threshold.

where: DANDI:001030 or 001032 to 001035 for the Figure 3A responses (assigned from their titles); the temperatures are calculated from the field, duration and conductivity, not measured
In [37]:
RHO_C = 4.18e6  # J per m3 per K, water (criterion)
cases = [("63 V/cm, NaCl", 63, 1.64, 2.5), ("63 V/cm, NaGlu", 63, 0.84, 1.24), ("81 V/cm, NaCl", 81, 1.64, 4.1)]
res = []
for name, e_vcm, sigma, paper in cases:
    for reading, fac in (("peak", 1.0), ("rms", 1 / np.sqrt(2))):
        e = e_vcm * 100 * fac
        dt = sigma * e ** 2 * 0.25 / RHO_C
        res.append(dict(case=name, reading=reading, rise_C=round(dt, 3), paper=paper,
                        within_10pct=abs(dt - paper) <= 0.1 * paper))
res = pd.DataFrame(res)
print(res.to_string(index=False))
r81 = (81 / 63) ** 2
rglu = 0.84 / 1.64
print(f"ratio 81/63 V/cm: formula {r81:.3f}, paper {4.1 / 2.5:.3f} (difference {100 * (4.1 / 2.5 / r81 - 1):.1f}%)")
print(f"ratio NaGlu/NaCl: formula {rglu:.3f}, paper {1.24 / 2.5:.3f} (difference {100 * (1.24 / 2.5 / rglu - 1):.1f}%)")
print(f"heat capacity that would give 2.5 C with the peak field: {1.64 * 6300 ** 2 * 0.25 / 2.5 / 1e6:.2f} MJ/m3/K; "
      f"with the RMS field: {1.64 * 6300 ** 2 / 2 * 0.25 / 2.5 / 1e6:.2f} MJ/m3/K")

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). Neither reading gives the paper's temperatures (peak field 3.89, 1.99 and 6.44 C; RMS field 1.95, 1.00 and 3.22 C, against 2.5, 1.24 and 4.1 C), while the paper's ratios follow the formula (81/63 V/cm within 0.8%, NaGlu/NaCl within 3.2%), which the criterion rules blocked. Getting 2.5 C would need a heat capacity of 6.51 MJ/m3/K with the peak field or 3.25 with the RMS field, against 4.18 for water.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The paper measured F over a soma outline drawn in ImageJ or MetaMorph on 64 x 64 images and identified APs by eye. The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no outline, so the claims file's Otsu ROIs (O1) and AP rule (O3) are used; the Otsu component is often a few pixels of bright membrane and the 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions. The readings also disagree within O1(a): in figs2-ttx-abolishes-aps and figs2-vehicle-keeps-response between the two pair readings O5, and in ap-amplitude-duration between its AP and duration readings (1 of 16 O1(a) readings within the paper's values). The claims file's measure of sustained depolarization (O4) asks for a plateau above 5 pre-stimulus SD or half the AP height with no AP in the last 100 ms; the plateaus in these data are lower (median 2.6% at the highest field, 1.15 to 6.01 points over the after-TTX and sham baseline), so the measure cannot detect them, and the claims that rest on it are blocked or fail for that reason (two not reproduced, as every reading fails). O4 also asks for no AP in the last 100 ms, where the paper describes APs that coalesce into small oscillations on top of the depolarization. Whether O1 and O4 suit these data is asked of a reader in questions/001271.yaml. The solution change of vehicle neurons is placed at the last gap over 3 minutes, which the files do not mark. The first and last frame of every file are left out.

What was found about the dataset. It holds the Figure S2 experiment: 6 TTX and 11 vehicle neurons with a visible solution change, 3 more vehicle-labelled neurons without one, and 5 sham sessions; no file is deposited twice. Its voltages give the fields of Figure S2 at 18 V/cm per V, not the 36 V/cm per V the files state. The TTX descriptions say TTX "caused sustained depolarization", where the paper and the dandiset description say it prevented it; the data side with the paper. Sessions before the change carry the same "vehicle control" label as vehicle sessions after it. The files hold no stimulus record, no ROI and frames of 16 x 16 pixels.
